title: The Pulse — September 15, 2026
tldr: Anthropic's Claude now writes 80% of their code, with engineers shipping 8x more per quarter. Meanwhile, the agent memory gap is getting defined: three new papers benchmark cross-session risks, inference budget constraints, and multi-agent orchestration trade-offs we're hitting in production.

models.title: DeepSeek Pro Latest and Flash Latest on OpenRouter
models.summary: DeepSeek's latest routing handles on OpenRouter: Pro at $0.66/$1.98 per million tokens, Flash (multimodal) at $0.15/$0.60, both with 1M context.
models.why: Competitive long-context pricing for retrieval and document agents where we route to the cheapest capable model.

research.title: MemRiskBench: Trace-Aware Risk-Preserving Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
research.summary: Benchmark for memory-specific risks in long-running agents: stale facts, conflicting updates, cross-user leakage, and constraint decay, with per-risk failure rates instead of aggregate scores.
research.why: Addresses exactly the durability and isolation issues we're architecting around in Pipeline's multi-tenant voice agents.

research.title: GraMRAG: Orchestrating Multi-Agent Multi-Step Reasoning via Graph Memory with Reinforcement Learning
research.summary: Graph-structured memory for multi-agent RAG with RL-driven orchestration; addresses state blindness in knowledge-intensive multi-step tasks.
research.why: Relevant pattern for coordinating document agents and maintaining shared retrieval state across turns.

research.title: LIMBO: Lifelong Inference-Time Memory and Budget Optimization for LLM Agents
research.summary: Balances what to replay from memory against per-call token budget; lifelong agents can't afford unbounded context growth.
research.why: The inference budget problem for stateful agents we hit every time context windows fill up mid-session.

research.title: Salesforce Koa: An Enterprise Language Model for Agentic Tool Use
research.summary: Salesforce fine-tuned Nemotron-3-Super-120B with GRPO on public and synthetic data for tool use and agentic workflows; no customer data used.
research.why: Tool-calling benchmark and training recipe relevant for SalesKick's agent stack.

research.title: MTAC-IFBench: Benchmarking Instruction-Following in Multi-Turn Agentic Coding
research.summary: Tests whether coding agents follow process constraints (no library X, test coverage above Y) across turns, not just functional correctness.
research.why: Exactly what we gate in PR review: adherence to repo rules and conventions, not just passing tests.

releases.title: Langfuse v4.36.0
releases.summary: AI gateway now relays authenticated OpenAI Realtime API requests; filter UI moved to inline suggestions; session timeline toggle; configurable event propagation block sizes.
releases.why: Langfuse is our observability layer; Realtime API support matters for Pipeline's voice agents, and event tuning helps with high-throughput logging.

hackernews.title: Pion, an agent designed to run any company autonomously
hackernews.summary: Andon Labs' autonomous company management agent pitch: cross-functional orchestration, continuous operation, and delegated decision-making.
hackernews.why: Worth knowing where the agent hype is pointing; no direct application yet, but instructive for scoping what 'autonomous' doesn't mean in practice.

hackernews.title: OpenAI bots knew about the RubyGems caching vulnerability
hackernews.summary: Public post describing how OpenAI's web crawler accessed and likely indexed a disclosed but not yet widely announced RubyGems cache poisoning bug.
hackernews.why: Reminder that scraping and training cut both ways: agents inherit knowledge, including security gotchas we haven't patched yet.

hackernews.title: How to write an effective software design document
hackernews.summary: Practical guide: problem, constraints, options, decision, and why; skip the filler, write it before the PR, update it when reality diverges.
hackernews.why: Reinforces the design-first workflow we're enforcing on larger features; agents can draft these now, and this is the template to hand them.

hackernews.title: Notes on gotchas while migrating 35kb preprompts from Opus to self-hosted Ollama
hackernews.summary: Field notes from a real migration: chunking, quality drop on reasoning, latency trade-offs, and which open models held up under production load.
hackernews.why: Relevant if we consider self-hosted fallback for high-volume low-margin endpoints; the gotchas are the actually useful part.

hackernews.title: GPT-5.6 Luna vs. GPT-6 Astra: Is a $1.20 Model Good Enough for Code Review?
hackernews.summary: Benchmark comparing Luna and Astra on code review tasks: Luna acceptable for routine checks, Astra better for architectural insight and subtle bugs.
hackernews.why: Directly applicable: we run wehshi with multi-model panels; knowing where cheaper models suffice saves us real money.

x_posts.title: Addy Osmani on Anthropic's agentic coding scale
x_posts.summary: Addy Osmani on Anthropic's internal CI scaling: Claude writes 80% of the code, engineers ship 8x more per quarter, tests grew 10x, CI jobs up 25x in six months.
x_posts.why: Real production numbers on agentic coding's blast radius; we're seeing the same test explosion and build time pressure.

x_posts.title: shadcn/lint: agent-first Tailwind linter
x_posts.summary: shadcn/lint announcement: agent-first linter for Tailwind; errors explain what broke and how to fix it using your design system's components and theme.
x_posts.why: Solves the agent-breaks-design-system problem we hit when agents freestyle CSS; constraint enforcement at lint time, not in PR review.

x_posts.title: Cline desktop app launch
x_posts.summary: Santiago on Cline's desktop app launch: agentic coding tools moving away from TUIs toward desktop apps with better affordances for multi-file, multi-step workflows.
x_posts.why: Pattern shift worth watching; we lean on terminal agents for CI and deploy, but richer UX might reduce the handoff friction.

x_posts.title: Hermes Business accounts
x_posts.summary: Nous Research announces Hermes Business: team accounts with shared balance, per-member caps, and shared skills that compound into proprietary IP.
x_posts.why: We're Hermes users; team accounts with shared skill libraries would centralize the runbooks and agent workflows we're building per client.

closing: Models: quiet day, only DeepSeek routing handles worth carrying. Next.js and Python: nothing notable in the window. DSPy, LangChain, Node: silent. Google's DevFest announcement and OpenAI's Fyxer and Perplexity case studies were vendor posts without new technical surface.
